A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GALLa. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained content against the additions in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on five code tasks, including multitask and single-task finetuning, graph ablations, and alternative adapters and encoders in Tables 3–7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, adds LLaMA2 and Qwen2.5-Coder evaluations in Table 3, and reports a model-output failure example in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The GNN–adapter–LLM architecture, Graph2Code and GraphQA objectives, and two-stage training procedure are retained. The new inference subsection explains the existing graph-free inference behavior; it does not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use CodeNet Python/Java graph-alignment data, CodefuseEval translation, and CodeXGLUE clone detection, defect detection, summarization, and repair. The represented languages and task requirements are unchanged; the added backbones do not introduce dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 substantially expands the evaluated baseline set by adding downstream-only finetuned LLaMA2 7B and Qwen2.5-Coder 1.5B/14B, each compared with GALLa variants across the retained tasks. All four original backbone baselines remain.

E3.justification: The added evaluations introduce full finetuning of Qwen2.5-Coder 1.5B and rank-64 LoRA training of LLaMA2 7B and Qwen2.5-Coder 14B. Existing data splits, metrics, epoch budgets, learning rates, and checkpoint selection remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D and Figure 7 add an illustrative failure analysis: a model trained with single-task finetuning answers a translation request with an unrelated graph statement. The existing AST/DFG, code-only, adapter, encoder, and single-task analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use chi-squared tests for discrete-task results, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests for summarization, and the same p < 0.1 reporting threshold. The statistical discussion moves to Appendix C; additional p-value rows use the existing practice, with no new run-count, seed, or uncertainty-estimation information.

E6.justification: v2 adds results and corresponding p-values for three backbones across the retained tasks. For example, the new Qwen2.5-Coder 14B rows report averages of 42.3 for the baseline, 44.2 for Graph2Code, and 46.0 for Graph2Code plus GraphQA. Original main results, single-task scores, ablation scores, and p-values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The architectural equations, training-objective expressions, and AST/DFG/UAST definitions are retained. Revised explanations and examples introduce no substantive mathematical definition, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of model/task-agnostic graph alignment, cross-language transfer, and no additional inference cost. Updating validation from four backbones up to 8B to seven up to 14B expands supporting evidence without redefining these central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds a template-copying explanation for single-task failures and states that multitask finetuning mitigates them. It also explains inference choices through graph-extraction latency and syntactic-completeness requirements, and newly acknowledges limitations concerning comparison methods, model scale, and task-specific hyperparameter searches.

D1.justification: v1 gives approximate GraphQA template counts and promises a future code release. v2 supplies actual question/answer templates, placeholder substitution and random-placement details in Appendix B, reports a released project-specific repository, and adds a dataset access link. These substantially expand documented reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 adds the LLaMA2 and Qwen2.5-Coder references. It changes the TransCoder-IR contrast from providing different information to providing limited structural information, and explicitly asserts first-work positioning for graph-enhanced decoder-only LLMs in Limitations. The broader related-work organization remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 adds an inference subsection, ablation paragraph headings, limitations and other closing sections, and prompt/failure appendices. GraphQA construction details and statistical explanations move into appendices, alongside localized method and related-work rewrites. The overall narrative and section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands displayed supporting material with prompt-template Figures 4–6 and the code/output example in Figure 7. It expands the main-result and p-value tables and merges v1's separate MLP/MagNet Tables 6–7 into Table 6. Figure 3 moves and its caption corrects 'without the code' to 'without the graph.'

improvement.justification: The additional backbone comparisons strengthen empirical support, while explicit GraphQA templates, specific code/data access information, and the failure example improve reproducibility and interpretation. v1 already contained the central experiments and ablations, so these are incremental overall gains. Small editorial defects, including Section 4.3 referring to five models despite Table 3 showing seven, do not outweigh the improvements.
